summary: The White Castle is a mid-weight worker-placement game set in feudal Japan, where players roll and place worker dice to gather resources, advance along tracks, and meld cards into combos, all while racing to be first through key milestones. It plays briskly for its depth, with tension coming from contested worker-placement spots and a shared area-movement track around the castle.
praised: clean, elegant integration of dice-as-workers with card melding
quick turns and low downtime for the genre
good tension from limited worker-placement spots and race elements
criticised: scoring can feel a bit fiddly to track
less thematic depth once the mechanisms are learned
worker-placement conflicts can occasionally lock a player out of a needed action

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking and area-movement race
interaction.detail: Players compete for the same limited worker-placement spaces each round and race along a shared circular track around the castle, which can block or slow opponents, while resource and card development otherwise sit on each player's own tableau.

scoring.how_you_win: Players place dice-workers around the castle to gain resources and climb four court tracks while contesting regional influence; the game ends when a track is topped out or the round limit is reached, and the player with the highest combined track and influence score wins.
